trigger: the 30s quiesce bound's justification (connect(5s)+write(10s)+read(10s)=25s legitimate worst case) is disproven
summary: Disproven three independent ways: (1) httplib.h SocketStream::wait_readable/wait_writable apply timeouts PER select() call, not as a cumulative request deadline; max_timeout_msec_ (the only mechanism that would make it cumulative) defaults to 0 and neither store calls set_max_timeout(). (2) issue #3017 documents this exact per-call-not-connection-lifetime behavior for this library version on the write path. (3) offload_target_store.cpp's OWN destructor comment in the SAME commit directly contradicts server.cpp's claim ('httplib's read/write timeouts reset PER CALL... a slow-dribbling remote endpoint can hold a delivery open well past 15s'). A slow-but-legitimate endpoint can hold deliver_single() open indefinitely, meaning the 30s bound could fire std::_Exit(1) (skipping all remaining teardown) on exactly the 'ordinary slow-but-healthy delivery' scenario the prior commit's message claimed to have fixed. independent_reporters=2: unhappy-path (3261-unhappy-p3-1) reached the same core conclusion independently via a different angle (queue-depth math rather than the httplib-source read), same pass, could not see each other's report.

Inconsistent with this same commit's own store_worker_pool.hpp::worker_loop(), which wraps spdlog calls in try/catch for exactly this reason.

(1d) upgrading.md's stacked-bound doc (~55s, telling operators to size grace period accordingly) goes stale and actively misleading the moment this stage is added without updating it — round-1's identical sequential 15+15 shape had the same doc-staleness gap but a softer consequence (leak-and-continue vs round-2's hard _Exit).

Traced the exact ctor-exception-safety question independently: db_ opened in the constructor BODY (not member-init), so a pool_ ctor throw during member-init happens before there is anything to leak. Confirmed no background thread starts earlier in ServerImpl's constructor that could race a not-yet-constructed store. Confirmed the rethrow propagates cleanly to main.cpp's existing top-level try/catch, exiting cleanly (no std::terminate). Matches cpp-safety's independent confirmation of the same fact (3261-cpps-p3-pass).

Force-exit's fixed stderr message is the only distinguishing signal from ordinary EXIT_FAILURE (same exit code 1 as most mundane startup/config-error paths), and the original message didn't say WHICH store (webhook, offload, or both) failed to drain, even with stderr captured.

The constructor exception-safety fix (this commit's headline change) has zero test coverage and, at time of finding, no tracked follow-up naming it specifically (only the quiesce-timeout escalate branch was tracked via #3280). Admittedly hard to test without an injectable thread-factory seam. Scope-extended into #3280 via issue comment rather than filing a new issue, per this reporter's own and cpp-safety's recommendation.

No race or lost guarantee from semaphore removal. Pool caps concurrent execution at 4, strictly under the removed semaphores' 10-permit limit, confirmed dead code. Grepped tests/ repo-wide for delivery_semaphore/offload_semaphore/SemaGuard/counting_semaphore — only a documentation cross-reference hit, no functional dependency. deliver_single() runs inside worker_loop()'s own try/catch net regardless of the removal.
